title: Stravinsky's story: music first, film second
summary: A story of Stravinsky refusing to write after the film was shot.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: You told a wonderful story once about Igor Stravinsky’s experience with being asked to write a film score.
Would you share that with us? It’s a charming story.

The story goes that Igor Stravinsky was approached to write a film score and had a meeting of minds with the power structure and the powers-to-be on the film project. They proceeded to tell Mr. Stravinsky, "Mr. Stravinsky, here’s how it works. We shoot the movie. We cast the movie. We go on location and shoot the movie and film it. Then we spend a great deal of time editing that movie. That’s a very complex, time-consuming process. After that, we call you to write the music for this movie." Igor Stravinsky says, "Oh, no. That won’t work. I will write the music first, and you will shoot the film afterwards. Your film will go according to my music, not the other way around."
No, that won’t work. Music first, film second.
